cases.raw_symptoms: A 55-year-old man had rheumatic fever with a temperature of 102°F, accompanied by pain and swelling of the joints and pain in the muscles attached to the affected joints, which were aggravated by touch and motion. He experienced great thirst, constipation, dryness and a constricted feeling in the throat, with throat pain extending to the ears. His urine was scanty, hot, and yellow in color. He also suffered from great weakness, violent headache, chill, and shivering of the body

physical.symptom: Arthritis with swelling and muscular pain

general.symptom: High fever (102°F) with chill and shivering

categorised.clinical_summary: A 55-year-old male presenting with acute rheumatic fever characterized by intense joint inflammation, high fever with thirst, and systemic dryness, suggesting a state of acute inflammatory stasis.

cases.clinical_notes: The strange, rare, and peculiar feature is the combination of intense systemic dryness (thirst, scanty urine) with the specific modality of aggravation from the slightest motion, pointing directly to the serous membrane inflammation characteristic of Bryonia.
